page: Amazon Web Services m7a.12xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core tests placing the instance in the top 10% of evaluated systems. Single-core performance and memory bandwidth across both small and large blocks rank in the top 25%. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and cryptography, as evidenced by its high Passmark scores and Redis SET operations throughput of 115.33 million operations per second. Large-model LLM inference speeds and single-threaded compression tasks perform in the average range.

From a resource density perspective, the m7a.12xlarge offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1:4, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high multi-core compute capacity without the premium of memory-optimized configurations. The absence of local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, focusing the instance's value on raw x86 CPU execution and network-based storage architectures. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate machine learning inference tasks.
